title: Latency scrapbook — quick run ledger
content:
Purpose:
- lightweight personal ledger to capture short experiments on p50/p95 and cost tradeoffs while iterating on batching + kv-cache heuristics. not canonical — quick notes that I can grep later.

Layout (columns):
Date 	 RunID 	 Model 	 Variant 	 BatchSize 	 AvgSeq 	 Tokens 	 p50_ms 	 p95_ms 	 cost_per_1k_tokens 	 notes

Rows:
2026-02-10	 26-02-A 	 llama2-13b	 fp16	 8	 128	 10240	 42	 110	 $0.32 	 baseline after kernel tweak; small tail spike at 10k tokens queued; need warmup tweak
2026-02-11	 26-02-B 	 llama2-13b	 fp16+kv-cache	 8	 128	 10240	 36	 88	 $0.28 	 KV prefix cache reduced p95 ~20%; memory healthy; observe slight jitter on concurrent small reqs
2026-02-12	 26-02-C 	 llama2-13b	 int8	 8	 128	 10240	 48	 140	 $0.18 	 quantization reduced cost but increased tail latency; investigate matmul kernel path
2026-02-14	 26-02-D 	 mpt-30b	 fp16	 4	 256	 10240	 85	 230	 $0.75 	 heavy memory pressure; experiment aborted after OOM on 1/20 runs
2026-02-18	 26-02-E 	 llama2-13b	 fp16	 dynamic-batch(4-16)	 120	 9600	 39	 95	 $0.29 	 dynamic batching helps p50 but p95 similar; check batching pad-inefficiency
2026-02-20	 26-02-F 	 llama2-13b	 fp16+kv-smart	 8	 128	 10240	 33	 74	 $0.27 	 introduced TTL 30s for prefix cache — hits up from 12%->28%; good improvement

Quick observations (free-form):
- kv-cache heuristic: TTL tradeoff is nice — higher hit rate reduces p95, but watch memory fragmentation. try slab allocator options next.
- quantization: int8 gives cost win but increases variance; likely because of slower fallback kernels for certain ops. add microprofiling for matmul vs attention kernels.
- batching windows: dynamic batching parameterization (min-window, max-window, max-delay-ms) needs to be tuned per route. small interactive routes prefer smaller max-delay.
- warmup: consistent p95 spikes at beginning of runs; consider adaptive warmup that pins a hot batch for the first N requests.

TODO (short):
- [ ] run matmul-only microprofile for int8 path (PR #912) — compare TF32 vs int8 kernel times
- [ ] test slab allocator setting A and B on staging host infra-7
- [ ] add a lightweight dashboard: rolling p50/p95 vs KV hit% for last 30m (small grafana panel)
- [ ] convert high-signal runs to formal bench spreadsheet and link to Confluence

Notes to self / shorthand log:
- 26-02-A: weird GC noise between 10:23-10:25, cross-check with infra SRE logs (node reclaim?).
- 26-02-C: int8 tail appears only on long sequences (>512) — low-seq behaviour is fine.
- 26-02-F: TTL=30s hit% jump likely due to synthetic workload pattern; need to test with real-prod traces.

Mini analysis snapshot (one-liner):
- Best p95 reduction for modest cost increase: fp16 + kv-smart + TTL tuning. Quantization needs kernel improvements before it's a net-win for tail latency.

References / quick links (for later):
- convo: #serving-runtime-kv-cache (Slack thread)
- ticket: JIRA-INF-4876 (dynamic-batching follow-up)
- PR: runtime/pull/912 (int8 kernel changes)

End of sheet — ephemeral, append-only until I refactor into a canonical bench doc.
